task: A small cinema desk wants a quick way to explore its film list. Using a six-film sample small enough to read in one look, build the code that searches titles, keeps one genre, adds up the stars, ranks the films and writes that ranking to a file.

produce.name: explore.py
produce.about: Search, genre filter, star totals, the ranking and the report writer.

produce.name: main.py
produce.about: Runs each step on the film file and prints its result.

produce.name: report.txt
produce.about: Every title in ranking order, one per line.

steps.P02.m1: Find titles that contain some text, ignoring case.
steps.P02.m2: Keep the films in one genre, sorted A to Z.
steps.P02.m3: Add up a genre's stars and count its films.
steps.P02.m4: Rank the films by stars, breaking ties A to Z.
steps.P02.m5: Write the ranking to a file, one title per line.

problems: Three of the six films have 5 stars, so the ranking needs a tie-break.
Stars are stored as text, so they must be turned into numbers before adding or sorting.
Titles start with capitals, so a search typed in capitals only matches when case is ignored.
